front: Bonjour, j'ai une ordonnance à vous donner.
pronunciation: [bohn-ZHOOR, zhay ün or-doh-NAHNS ah voo doh-NAY]
back: Hello, I have a prescription for you.
context: Give the 'ordonnance' and your Carte Vitale to the pharmacist.

front: Vous avez quelque chose contre le mal de gorge ?
pronunciation: [voo zah-vay kel-kuh shohz kohn-truh luh mahl duh GORZH]
back: Do you have something for a sore throat?
context: 'Contre' = against, for (a symptom).

front: Ce médicament est disponible sans ordonnance.
pronunciation: [suh may-dee-kah-MAHN eh dees-poh-NEE-bluh sahn zor-doh-NAHNS]
back: This medicine is available without a prescription.
context: In France, even basic medicines are sold in pharmacies, not supermarkets.

front: Prenez deux comprimés toutes les six heures.
pronunciation: [pruh-nay duh kohm-pree-MAY toot lay see ZUHR]
back: Take two tablets every six hours.
context: 'Un comprimé' = tablet; 'une gélule' = capsule; 'un sirop' = syrup.

front: À prendre pendant les repas.
pronunciation: [ah PRAHN-druh pahn-dahn lay ruh-PAH]
back: To be taken with meals.
context: Typical instructions on medicine boxes.

front: Est-ce qu'il y a des effets secondaires ?
pronunciation: [es-keel yah day zeh-feh suh-kohn-DEHR]
back: Are there any side effects?
context: 'Les effets secondaires' = side effects.

front: Ne dépassez pas la dose prescrite.
pronunciation: [nuh day-pah-say pah lah dohz pres-KREET]
back: Do not exceed the prescribed dose.
context: Warning on every medicine leaflet ('la notice').

front: Vous avez la version générique ?
pronunciation: [voo zah-vay lah vehr-syohn zhay-nay-REEK]
back: Do you have the generic version?
context: French pharmacists often substitute generics automatically.

front: Je me suis fait piquer par un moustique, ça me gratte.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee feh pee-kay par an moos-TEEK, sah muh GRAT]
back: I got bitten by a mosquito, it itches.
context: 'Se faire piquer' = to get bitten/stung (se faire + infinitive = to get something done to you). 'Ça gratte' = it itches.

front: Il me faudrait une crème solaire indice cinquante.
pronunciation: [eel muh foh-dreh ün krem soh-lehr an-dees san-KAHNT]
back: I'd need a factor 50 sunscreen.
context: 'Il me faudrait' = I'd need. 'Indice' = SPF.

front: Le pharmacien m'a conseillé de voir un médecin.
pronunciation: [luh far-mah-SYAN mah kohn-seh-YAY duh vwahr an mayd-SAN]
back: The pharmacist advised me to see a doctor.
context: French pharmacists give a lot of health advice for free.

front: Je viens chercher un colis.
pronunciation: [zhuh vyan shehr-shay an koh-LEE]
back: I've come to pick up a parcel.
context: 'Venir chercher' = to come and pick up.

front: J'ai reçu un avis de passage.
pronunciation: [zhay ruh-sü an nah-vee duh pah-SAHZH]
back: I got a delivery notice.
context: Left when nobody was home: you then collect the parcel at the post office or a relay point.

front: Voici ma pièce d'identité.
pronunciation: [vwah-SEE mah pyes dee-dahn-tee-TAY]
back: Here's my ID.
context: 'Une pièce d'identité' = ID document.

front: Je voudrais envoyer ce colis au Brésil.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh ahn-vwah-yay suh koh-LEE oh bray-ZEEL]
back: I'd like to send this parcel to Brazil.
context: 'Envoyer' = to send.

front: En lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [ahn leh-truh ruh-koh-mahn-DAY ah-vek ah-kü-zay duh ray-sep-SYOHN, seel voo PLEH]
back: By registered mail with proof of receipt, please.
context: Essential in France for official letters, e.g. ending a lease or a contract.

front: Il faut combien de timbres pour l'étranger ?
pronunciation: [eel foh kohm-byan duh TAN-bruh poor lay-trahn-ZHAY]
back: How many stamps do I need for abroad?
context: 'Un timbre' = stamp.

front: Le colis pèse deux kilos.
pronunciation: [luh koh-LEE pez duh kee-LOH]
back: The parcel weighs two kilos.
context: 'Peser' = to weigh: il pèse (accent grave).

front: Il y a un point relais près de chez moi.
pronunciation: [eel yah an pwan ruh-LEH preh duh shay MWAH]
back: There's a parcel pick-up point near my place.
context: 'Un point relais' = a shop where you collect online orders.

front: Je voudrais suivre mon colis.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh SWEE-vruh mohn koh-LEE]
back: I'd like to track my parcel.
context: 'Suivre' = to follow, track. 'Le numéro de suivi' = tracking number.

front: Le facteur est déjà passé ?
pronunciation: [luh fak-tuhr eh day-zhah pah-SAY]
back: Has the mail carrier come yet?
context: 'Le facteur / la factrice' = mail carrier.

front: Il faut remplir ce formulaire de douane.
pronunciation: [eel foh rahm-pleer suh for-mü-lehr duh DWAN]
back: You need to fill out this customs form.
context: 'La douane' = customs.

front: Je voudrais faire une réclamation, mon colis n'est jamais arrivé.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh fehr ün ray-klah-mah-SYOHN, mohn koh-lee neh zhah-meh zah-ree-VAY]
back: I'd like to make a complaint, my parcel never arrived.
context: 'Une réclamation' = complaint (formal).

front: La poste ferme entre midi et quatorze heures.
pronunciation: [lah POST fehrm ahn-truh mee-DEE ay kah-tor-ZUHR]
back: The post office closes between noon and 2 p.m.
context: Small post offices often close at lunchtime.

front: Il faut faire une demande de passeport à la mairie.
pronunciation: [eel foh fehr ün duh-mahnd duh pas-POR ah lah meh-REE]
back: You have to apply for a passport at the town hall.
context: 'Faire une demande' = to apply. 'La mairie' handles many paperwork tasks.

front: J'ai rendez-vous à la préfecture pour mon titre de séjour.
pronunciation: [zhay rahn-day-VOO ah lah pray-fek-TÜR poor mohn tee-truh duh say-ZHOOR]
back: I have an appointment at the prefecture for my residence permit.
context: 'La préfecture' handles residence permits ('titres de séjour') for foreigners.

front: Il manque une pièce à votre dossier.
pronunciation: [eel mahnk ün PYES ah voh-truh doh-SYAY]
back: One document is missing from your file.
context: 'Une pièce' here = a document. 'Il manque' = there is missing.

front: Revenez avec une photocopie de votre passeport.
pronunciation: [ruh-vuh-nay ah-vek ün foh-toh-koh-PEE duh voh-truh pas-POR]
back: Come back with a photocopy of your passport.
context: Bureaucracy in France often means a second visit!

front: Le délai de traitement est de deux mois.
pronunciation: [luh day-leh duh tret-mahn eh duh duh MWAH]
back: The processing time is two months.
context: 'Le délai' = time frame, deadline.

front: Prenez un ticket et attendez votre tour.
pronunciation: [pruh-nay an tee-KEH ay ah-tahn-day voh-truh TOOR]
back: Take a ticket and wait your turn.
context: 'Votre tour' = your turn.

front: C'est à quel guichet ?
pronunciation: [seh tah kel ghee-SHEH]
back: Which counter is it?
context: 'Le guichet' = counter, window.

front: Vous devez joindre un justificatif.
pronunciation: [voo duh-vay ZHWAN-druh an zhüs-tee-fee-kah-TEEF]
back: You must attach supporting documents.
context: 'Joindre' = to attach (to a file or email).

front: Toutes les démarches se font maintenant en ligne.
pronunciation: [toot lay day-MARSH suh fohn mant-nahn ahn LEEN]
back: All procedures are now done online.
context: 'Les démarches (administratives)' = paperwork, procedures.

front: J'ai passé la matinée à faire de la paperasse.
pronunciation: [zhay pah-say lah mah-tee-nay ah fehr duh lah pah-PRAS]
back: I spent the morning doing paperwork.
context: 'La paperasse' = paperwork (slightly negative).

front: Merci, bonne fin de journée !
pronunciation: [mehr-SEE, bun fan duh zhoor-NAY]
back: Thanks, have a good rest of the day!
context: A typical goodbye at a counter in the afternoon.
